answer_1.quote: To handle the chit-chat task, we train a conditional language model that intakes dialogue history and generates a context-aware response.
answer_1.outputs: Generated dialogue responses containing recommended item mentions

answer_2.quote: We report perplexity (PPL) and distinct n-grams (DIST), assessing the fluency and the diversity of generated responses, respectively. We also employ a top‑k evaluation approach with k values of 1, 10, and 50 and report Recall@k (R@k), Recall in Response (ReR@k), Precision in Response (PrR@k) and their harmonic mean F1@k.

answer_4.quote: We engaged three annotators who were tasked with assessing model outputs given a dialogue history. 100 model outputs from each model are randomly sampled... The annotators score each model output from the range of 0 to 2 on the level of informativeness, coherence, and fluency of model output.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were instructed to evaluate fluency (naturalness and grammaticality), informativeness (accuracy and completeness of information), and coherence (integration with the conversation flow) on a 0‑2 scale.
